title: Primacy of Existence
summary: The universe exists independent of consciousness. Consciousness apprehends. It does not decree.

lessons.title: Independent of consciousness
lessons.objective: State that the universe exists whether or not anyone is aware of it.

exercises.prompt: On the primacy of existence, what does the universe depend on?

choices.text: Nothing in consciousness. It exists on its own.
Someone noticing it.
A wish that it be there.
Agreement that it is real.

feedback.note: The universe exists independent of consciousness. Awareness is not what keeps it in being.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to whether it fits independence.

pairs.left: A mountain is there with no one looking
A fact waits on a mind to exist
The universe was real before any awareness

feedback.note: Independence means existence does not start when a mind shows up.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit line about the universe.

feedback.note: The key word is independent. Consciousness is not the ground of the universe.

exercises.prompt: Build the order that primacy of existence uses.

feedback.note: Existence comes first. Being noticed is not a condition of existing.

exercises.prompt: A star no one has ever seen still exists. What does that show?

choices.text: Existence does not need a knower.
Unseen things are not real.
The star exists only in a possible mind.
It starts to exist when someone finds it.

feedback.note: Finding a fact is not what makes the fact. The fact was already there.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its place under primacy of existence.

feedback.note: What is comes first. A wish is not a foundation for it.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

feedback.note: Reality does not wait to be acknowledged before it is real.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states primacy of existence?

choices.text: The universe exists independent of consciousness.
The universe exists only inside a mind.
Consciousness makes the universe by thinking.
The universe exists when enough people agree.

feedback.note: The unit sentence is independence, not a mind-made world.

exercises.prompt: Put the denial in the right order.

feedback.note: A knower is not a requirement of existence.

exercises.prompt: If every conscious being vanished, what would primacy of existence say about the rocks?

choices.text: They would still exist.
They would stop existing.
They would become mere ideas.
They would pause until a new mind arrived.

feedback.note: Independence means the rocks do not need witnesses.

lessons.title: Consciousness apprehends
lessons.objective: Say what consciousness does: it takes in what exists. It does not create it.

exercises.prompt: Under this unit, what is the job of consciousness?

choices.text: To apprehend what exists.
To bring the universe into being.
To decide which facts are allowed.
To have no object at all.

feedback.note: Consciousness apprehends. Taking in is not the same as creating.

exercises.prompt: Match each act to the right description.

pairs.right: Trying to rule reality by a mind
Leaving a fact unseen, not unreal

feedback.note: Apprehension reaches a fact. A decree would pretend to set the fact.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second line of the unit.

feedback.note: The verb for consciousness here is apprehends, not invents.

exercises.prompt: Build what consciousness does.

feedback.note: It takes in what exists. Creating is the distractor this unit rejects.

exercises.prompt: You look at a table. On this view, looking does what?

choices.text: It apprehends a table that is already there.
It brings the table into existence.
It makes the table optional.
It decrees the table’s identity.

feedback.note: Seeing is apprehension of something that does not depend on the seeing.

exercises.prompt: Match the mind’s role to the case.

pairs.right: Not a way to unmake it

feedback.note: Notice takes the storm in. The wish does not cancel it, and the storm did not need the notice.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

feedback.note: Grasping and creating are different jobs. Only grasping belongs to consciousness here.

exercises.prompt: Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Existence is independent. Consciousness apprehends.
Existence apprehends. Consciousness is the universe.
Both existence and consciousness decree facts.
Neither exists until a theory is written.

feedback.note: Keep the two roles apart: the universe is independent, and consciousness apprehends it.

exercises.prompt: Order the two jobs.

tokens.text: then the mind invents the universe

feedback.note: Apprehension follows what is. It does not open existence.

exercises.prompt: A mistake in awareness means what, on this unit?

choices.text: The mind failed to apprehend what is there.
The fact changed to match the mistake.
The object stopped existing.
Error and reality are the same thing.

feedback.note: A miss is a failure of apprehension, not a rewrite of the object.

lessons.title: It does not decree
lessons.objective: Reject the idea that wishing, believing, or agreeing can rewrite what exists.

exercises.prompt: What does consciousness not do?

choices.text: It does not decree reality.
It does not apprehend anything.
It does not exist at all.
It cannot ever be mistaken.

feedback.note: The unit line is direct: consciousness apprehends. It does not decree.

exercises.prompt: Match each attempt to the result under this unit.

pairs.left: Believing two and two are five

feedback.note: Wish, belief, and agreement do not decree what exists.

exercises.prompt: Complete the refusal.

feedback.note: Decree is the act this unit denies to consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Build the short formula.

feedback.note: Hold both halves: apprehension is real, and decree is refused.

exercises.prompt: A crowd agrees the river is dry while it floods the road. What is true?

choices.text: The flood is real. Agreement does not decree otherwise.
The agreement makes the river dry.
The river is dry for them and flooded in itself, both fully.
Without a decree, water cannot exist.

feedback.note: Numbers of minds do not turn a flood into a dry road.

exercises.prompt: Match the mental act to what it can and cannot do.

pairs.right: Is a decree, and it fails

feedback.note: Only apprehension fits the mind’s role. Denial and orders do not rewrite the water.

exercises.prompt: Fill the limit on belief.

feedback.note: Belief can be an attempt to apprehend. It is not a decree that creates the fact.

exercises.prompt: Which is a decree, and therefore rejected here?

choices.text: My wanting it is what makes it true.
I look in order to find out what is true.
I can fail to notice a fact.
The fact was there before I asked.

feedback.note: Treating a want as the maker of truth is the decree this unit refuses.

exercises.prompt: Order the rejection.

feedback.note: Wanting is not a power to edit existence.

exercises.prompt: Why is “consciousness decrees” the wrong slogan?

choices.text: It gives the mind a power this unit denies.
It means the same as apprehend.
It says the mind is too weak to notice anything.
It says the universe does not exist.

feedback.note: Decree would make consciousness the ruler of facts. Primacy of existence says it is not.

lessons.title: Two opposite claims
lessons.objective: Tell primacy of existence apart from the claim that consciousness comes first and sets the facts.

exercises.prompt: Which claim is primacy of existence?

choices.text: Existence is independent, and consciousness apprehends it.
Consciousness comes first and decrees what exists.
Existence and a wish are the same thing.
Neither existence nor consciousness is real.

feedback.note: Primacy of existence puts the universe first. The opposite puts a decree first.

exercises.prompt: Match each slogan to the claim it states.

pairs.left: The universe exists independent of consciousness

feedback.note: Two lines belong to this unit. The decree line is the opposite claim.

exercises.prompt: Name the view this unit teaches.

parts.text: The view is the primacy of

feedback.note: The name is primacy of existence, not primacy of a wish or a decree.

exercises.prompt: Build the opposite claim so you can reject it.

tokens.text: and that claim is this unit

feedback.note: Naming the opposite helps you keep it out of the unit. This unit does not adopt it.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, “If I do not think of the tree, the tree is nothing.” Which claim is that?

choices.text: The opposite of primacy of existence.
Primacy of existence itself.
A plain case of apprehending.
A statement that the tree is independent.

feedback.note: Tying the tree’s being to a thought makes consciousness primary. This unit says the tree does not need the thought.

exercises.prompt: Sort each line.

pairs.left: Facts do not need a knower
To be is to be perceived

feedback.note: Keep independence and apprehension on one side, and perception-as-being and wanting-as-making on the other.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast in one line.

feedback.note: What is primary is existence, not a mental decree.

exercises.prompt: How do you test a slogan against this unit?

choices.text: Ask whether it makes existence depend on a mind’s decree.
Ask which slogan is said more loudly.
Ask which slogan is older.
Ask which slogan feels kinder.

feedback.note: The test is dependence. If a mind must decree the fact, the slogan is not this unit.

exercises.prompt: State the test in order.

tokens.text: If a mind must decree the fact
the slogan is not primacy of existence

feedback.note: A required decree fails the test. Independence plus apprehension passes it.

lessons.title: Hold the unit
lessons.objective: Put the three lines together: independent existence, apprehension, and no decree.

exercises.prompt: Which set is the whole unit?

choices.text: The universe is independent. Consciousness apprehends. It does not decree.
Only that wishes sometimes come true.
Only that minds do not exist.
The universe obeys whatever is believed.

feedback.note: All three lines are one unit. Dropping independence or smuggling in a decree breaks it.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to its job in the unit.

feedback.note: Each line has one job. Together they are primacy of existence.

exercises.prompt: Restore the summary.

parts.text: The universe exists independent of consciousness. Consciousness

feedback.note: The two verbs stay in that order: apprehends, then the refusal to decree.

exercises.prompt: Build the three lines in unit order.

tokens.text: The universe exists independent of consciousness

feedback.note: Order: independence, then apprehension, then the refusal to decree.

exercises.prompt: You learn a fact you dislike. What does the unit tell you to do?

choices.text: Apprehend it. Dislike does not decree it away.
Decree that the fact stop existing.
Gather votes until the fact changes.
Treat the universe as dependent on your dislike.

feedback.note: Dislike is not a decree. The fact stays independent, and the mind’s job is to apprehend it.

exercises.prompt: Match the situation to the line it illustrates.

pairs.left: Announcing that the reading shall be otherwise

feedback.note: The planet needs no observer, the reading takes a fact in, and the announcement does not rewrite it.

exercises.prompt: Fill the one-line hold.

feedback.note: Independence and the ban on decree are the two edges of the same hold.

exercises.prompt: Which shortening still keeps the unit?

choices.text: What is does not depend on a mind, and a mind does not rule it.
Minds rule facts whenever they are sure.
Only decrees are real.
Nothing exists to apprehend.

feedback.note: The short form still has independence and the refusal to let a mind rule the facts.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit in order.

feedback.note: That is the whole hold: independent existence, apprehension, and no decree.

exercises.prompt: What would break the unit if you added it?

choices.text: A clause that lets consciousness decree an exception.
A reminder that apprehension can be careful.
A reminder that a mind can miss a fact.
A reminder that unseen facts still exist.

feedback.note: An exception that lets a mind decree would cancel primacy of existence. Care, error, and unseen facts do not.
